taxonomy.desc: Sources for Speaker and Organization Metadata: Sources for Speaker Names, Parties, Parliamentary Groups as well as Organization metadata. Multiple sources can describe one element.

category.catDesc: Parliaments Day-by-Day Database: The Parliaments Day-by-Day Database provides, among other things, date-specific party affiliation data for Germany, the Netherlands and Switzerland. For Germany, the initial data collection covers the party affiliation of MPs between 1949 and 2017. According to the online appendix of Turner-Zwinkels et al. 2022, it is based on the Stammdaten file of the German Bundestag (see #DE-source.stammdaten). We build on this collection and extend the database for the years 2017 to 2025 using party affiliation data from Wikipedia. The initial dataset can be found in the Harvard Dataverse and is licensed under the CC Zero license. The granularity of the data is date-specific for most party affiliations. The full reference to the dataset is Turner-Zwinkels, Tomas; Huywler, Oliver; Frech, Elena; Manow, Philip; Bailer, Stefanie; Goet, Niels; Hug, Simon (2021): "Parliaments day-by-day" [Dataset] V2. Harvard Dataverse.. The accompanying research article can be found at Turner-Zwinkels, Tomas; Huywler, Oliver; Frech, Elena; Manow, Philip; Bailer, Stefanie; Goet, Niels D.; Hug, Simon (2022): "Parliaments Day-by-Day: A New Open Source Database to Answer the Question of Who Was in What Parliament, Party, and Party-group, and When". In Legislative Studies Quarterly 47 (3): 761--784.

Protocols of the German Bundestag: If the date of the assumption of a particular office is unclear, the protocols of the German Bundestag were consulted to retrieve the date of a particular election or swearing in of a person.

Wikipedia: In particular for speakers who are not members of parliament, addtional metadata has been retrieved from Wikipedia. This concerns canonical names as well as party affiliation data. For governmental actors, presidential speakers (i.e., chair, vice-chair, president by the right of age), parliamentary commissioners and Presidents of Germany, an attempt was made to provide date-specific information on names, party affiliations and organizational affiliation where possible with Wikipedia. Provided dates only account for the time-spans these persons were in office (e.g., the party affiliation for governmnetal speakers is limited to the dates a particular person was in office and no assumptions are made on party affiliations beyond that). For other irregular speakers like guests as well as for representatives of the German Federal Council, the granularity of added metadata is on the level of legislative periods, resulting in less granular annotation of metadata. Wikipedia was also used as a source for metadata on organizations. For these, URLs are provided.

Stammdaten of the German Bundestag: An authoritative master file containing information of members of the German Bundestag from 1949 to 2025. It provides rich metadata on speakers including general biographical information as well as date-specific name changes and affiliations to parliamentary groups. It does not contain date-specific party affiliations which are added via the Parliaments Day-by-Day dataset and Wikipedia. The Stammdaten file can be retrieved from the Open Data Website of the German Bundestag. Used version: 1747280711. Note that information on "sex" is coded both static and binary in the Stammdaten file. To avoid gaps and overlaps in the time spans of names, some time spans were adjusted. Occassional incomplete time spans (in particular characterized by missing end dates for affiliations) were addressed by approximating the end date via the starting date of the next affiliation or the end of legislative periods.

Wikidata: Wikidata was used as the main source for IDs for speakers as well as for gender information on speakers who never have been members of parliament. Queried property for gender: "sex or gender" (P21).
